cheng: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on seqlen=64 workloads on a subset of SM92 nodes after the recent kernel-autotune rollout. Tail latency up ~30% on p95. Anyone else seeing this?

devon: Saw that on the dashboard earlier. Quick profiler dump (from one of the failing pods):
```
[profile] model=rwkv-small, seqlen=64, batch=1
kernel chosen: generic_attention_fp16
kernel time: 12.8ms (prev: 7.9ms)
memcpy H2D: 1.2ms (was 0.2ms)
KV-cache write stalls: 2.1ms
```

maria: Hmm — autotuner seems to have flipped to a non-tc-fused path even though the device advertises tensor cores. arch-detect output for that machine: 
```
$ ./arch-scan --device /dev/nv0
SM: 9.2
Driver: 537.12
TensorCores: true
FP16: true
BF16: false
FP8: experimental
quirks: iommu-flush, slow-pcie-link
```

maria: The BF16 flag is false, so our kernel selector rejected the bf16/tc fusion path and picked the fallback. But before the rollout we had a soft-fallback that allowed tc-fused fp16 when bf16 absent. Looks like autotune tightened the capability gate.

runtime-bot: [deploy] release/2026-03-15-autotune -> prod succeeded on cluster-a (sha: b1c2d3). Autotune config: kernel_weight=0.95, detect_strict=true

sahil: That strict detect flag is suspicious. If detect_strict=true, we require exact BF16 support for fused kernels — but on these SM92 cards fused fp16+tensorcore path is faster and safe. We should relax the gate for SM>=90 and non-bf16 devices.

devon: Repro script to confirm locally:
```sh
# reproduce slow path
./runtimerun --model rwkv-small --device /dev/nv0 --seqlen 64 --profile
# quick override to force tc-fused path
export RW_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=tc_fused_fp16
./runtimerun --model rwkv-small --device /dev/nv0 --seqlen 64 --profile
```

cheng: I ran the override on one node — latency drops back to 8.1ms and memcpy drops. So kernel correctness is fine; it's a gating/heuristic issue. But note KV-cache write stalls are higher when the kernel path does extra H2D churn. Could be microbatching/batching heuristic interplay.

maria: Here's the selector snippet that changed in the rollout (from the autotune patch):
```py
# old
if sm >= 90 and has_tensorcores:
    prefer = 'tc_fused_bf16' if has_bf16 else 'tc_fused_fp16'
# new (tighter)
if sm >= 90 and has_tensorcores and has_bf16:
    prefer = 'tc_fused_bf16'
else:
    prefer = 'generic_attention_fp16'
```

maria: So the new logic removed the 'tc_fused_fp16' branch. That explains it.

sahil: Proposal: revert the strict change and add debounce heuristics to avoid flip-flopping on marginal devices. Something like: keep last-chosen kernel for N minutes or N samples unless new kernel shows >10% improvement across a stable profiling window.

cheng: Agreed. Also add a capability probe tweak: record 'effective_tensorcore' if fused_fp16 kernel passes a short correctness microbench and latency wins. Then annotate device signature with "prefer_tc_fp16" to allow safe fastpath. This avoids relying solely on BF16 advertised flag which is inconsistent across drivers.

devon: Quick patch idea — add a per-device heuristic override in the runtime state:
```json
{"device_id": "nv0", "prefer_tc_fp16": true, "last_probe": 6601230000}
```

maria: Also observed KV-cache thrash when we switch kernels mid-flight. We should add a small KV-debounce window on kernel switches so we don't evict/warm KV repeatedly. E.g., dont switch kernel for an active shard unless 5m of stable telemetry.

runtime-bot: [ticket created] ENG-RUNTIME-1423 - autotune: reinstate tc_fused_fp16 branch + add kernel-debounce + device-probe microbench. Assigned to devon.

devon: I'll prepare a revert PR for the autotune gating and add the debounce state. Plan: revert config change + add microbench probe (30 requests warmup, measure end-to-end). If that passes on 10 devices with different PCIe quirks, we can re-enable weight.

cheng: Priority high. This is impacting some production routes (chat-small, realtime-infer). @sahil can you add a temporary routing policy to route seqlen<=64 to a conservative kernel group until we push the PR?

sahil: Yep — I'll add a routing override for the next 2 hours and monitor p95.

maria: Also, logging action item: add a metric 'kernel_picker_reason' (explicit_cap, microbench_pass, legacy_override) so we can triage similar flips next time.

cheng: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after PR review. Short notes: revert strict BF16 requirement, add microbench probe for tc_fp16, implement kernel switch debounce and KV-cache warmup window.

sahil: :thumbsup:
